summary.headline: MapmyIndia Q2 FY27: revenue up 15.8% YoY, EBITDA up 60%, PAT up 90%; management guides to EBITDA margin of 35%+ for FY27.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue growth of 15.8% YoY, EBITDA growth of 60% and PAT growth of 90%, with H1 revenue up 18.4%, EBITDA up 20.4% and PAT up 32%. Map-led and IoT-led both grew strongly, with Map-led at INR 76.7 crore revenue and IoT-led at INR 55.1 crore. Management attributed the government segment's sharp sequential/YoY drop to a one-off execution in the prior-year quarter, and said receivables (around 120-122 days) are a focus, mainly government collections of about INR 100 crore. Management declined to give numeric guidance for H2 beyond EBITDA margin, but said H2 should be better than H1 on the open order book.

financial_highlights.value: About INR 30 crore (analyst figure, not confirmed by management)
About INR 22 crore (analyst figure, not confirmed by management)
About INR 174-186 crore (analyst figures); receivable days around 120-122 (analyst reference), 133 days cited by analyst

segments.name: Map-led
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue of INR 76.7 crore with 41.6% EBITDA margin; H1 EBITDA margin of 47%.

segments.name: IoT-led
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue of INR 55.1 crore with 23.8% EBITDA margin; H1 EBITDA margin about 19.2%. Margin expansion attributed to operating leverage and group-wide IoT sales synergies.

segments.name: Automotive
segments.commentary: Grew about 52% in Q2 and about 40% in H1; wins included a localised navigation solution for commercial vehicles and a 2-wheeler OEM contract renewal.

segments.name: Enterprise
segments.commentary: Grew about 44% in Q2; wins in last-mile delivery, quick commerce and logistics, and a large workforce-automation software stack deal. An existing quick-commerce customer scaled volumes 5x.

segments.name: Government
segments.commentary: Revenue fell YoY against a one-off win in the prior-year quarter, but rose sequentially in Q2. New Go-Lives include oil and gas upstream digital twin and a first national disaster response win.

guidance_outlook: Management expects to maintain consolidated EBITDA margin of 35% or more; H1 FY27 EBITDA margin is 37.2%.
Management believes H2 FY27 can be better than H1 FY27, citing growth momentum and conversion of a substantial open order book.
Management said Q3 should be good as well as Q4, with a large oil and gas IoT government subscription contract now live and its subscriptions starting to flow.
Management declined to give a specific revenue growth number; said it is 'very encouraging and quite bullish' on returning to 20%+ growth but gave no figure.
Management said the company has not been impacted by geopolitical developments so far and has no visibility of any impact.
capex_capacity: No capex amounts, capacity expansion, or utilisation figures were discussed on the call.
Management said it is investing in technology 'in a big way for future readiness' and is embedding AI, ML and neural networks across Map-led and IoT-led platforms; no rupee capex quantum was given.
Inventory was said to have been brought down to half; supplier accounts are being settled faster and cash flows were described as strong.

Commissioning and go-live timelines discussed: a large oil and gas IoT government subscription contract has gone live and subscriptions have started to flow; oil and gas upstream digital twin and a first national disaster response win were cited as Go-Lives, with no dates or values.
demand_pricing: Strong funnel and open order book in enterprise and government, including defence; management declined to quantify the next-quarter growth.
Government: company is being selective in bids, seeking portfolio with collectability and margin, to avoid later issues.

Pricing and revenue models vary by customer: annual licence fees, delivery-based, per transaction, consumption-based, per asset/vehicle, per user per month. This drives seasonality (Enterprise peaks in Q1 and Q4; Government peaks towards Q4).
Data and API licensing grouped together as one revenue category; management said quarterly comparisons are misleading and should be viewed on a full-year basis.
IoT growth attributed to group-wide sales synergy, with automotive OEMs as a channel for IoT device sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why is enterprise revenue seasonality so high, with one quarter nearly doubling versus others?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited varied revenue models (annual licences, delivery-based, per transaction, per asset, per user-month) and different contract sizes, which drive the peaks.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 be better than H1, and what will drive it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 should be better than H1, given three quarters of growth and conversion of the open order book; it highlighted a large oil and gas IoT subscription contract going live.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth return to 20%+?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no number, but said visibility is encouraging and it is bullish, with large open-order contracts going live.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivable days elevated at 120-122 days, and are there non-government projects with long cycles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said non-government receivables are healthy and stable; the focus is on collecting roughly INR 100 crore of government receivables sooner.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving IoT margin expansion despite higher hardware sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited operating leverage on fixed costs, group-wide IoT sales synergy via automotive OEMs, inventory and cost optimisation, and growing SaaS follow-on revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the hardware and service revenue from IoT one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no one-off; device sales grow with customer count and should be viewed on an annual basis, not quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a geopolitical or other drag holding back growth acceleration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has not been affected by geopolitical events so far and sees no visibility of impact, but declined to give a revenue forecast.

risks_watch: Government receivables of roughly INR 100 crore and overall receivable days of about 120-122; collection progress next quarter.
Government revenue lumpiness and one-off base effects; selective bidding may limit near-term government growth.
Revenue growth (18.4% in H1) lagging the 20%+ growth the analyst asked about; management gave no numeric target.
Margin sustainability: IoT-led margin 23.8% in Q2 versus 19.2% in H1 depends on hardware volume and operating leverage.
Management did not quantify H2 revenue; watch for Q3 delivery on open order book and the oil and gas IoT subscription ramp.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, momentum and EBITDA margin, but evasive and non-committal when asked for specific revenue numbers, H2 growth quantum or acceleration timelines. Management repeatedly deflected numeric questions to the yearly view and cited that results will only be known after quarter-end.
key_quotes: Our growth for half year is almost 18.4% in the H1.
We are trying to see that we maintain EBITDA margin of 35% plus.
So far, we have not been impacted by the geopolitical scenario so far.
Look at it on a yearly basis.

growth.why: Management gave no numeric revenue growth guidance beyond holding EBITDA margin at 35%+ for FY27 and saying H2 should be better than H1 on an open order book and a large oil and gas IoT subscription contract now live; no capacity additions or capex were discussed.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management is guiding to maintain consolidated EBITDA margin at 35%+ for FY27 versus H1 at 37.2%, with IoT-led margin rising to 23.8% in Q2 from 19.2% in H1 on operating leverage and group IoT synergies.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No capacity expansion, plant or capex timing was discussed on the call.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management said H2 should be better than H1 on a substantial open order book and a large oil and gas IoT subscription now live, though it gave no numeric growth figure and H1 revenue grew only 18.4%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex quantum or utilisation figures were given; management only said it is investing in technology and AI without a rupee amount.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to give any numeric revenue guidance and gave no figure for returning to 20%+ growth, so there is no stated base to raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Roughly INR 100 crore of government receivables and 120-122 receivable days are unresolved, and selective government bidding may limit near-term growth after a one-off prior-year base.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product or model launches were named; the call covered AI and ML embedding in existing Map-led and IoT-led platforms only.

rows.label: Oil and gas IoT subscription ramp
rows.why: A large oil and gas IoT government subscription contract is already live and management said subscriptions are starting to flow, supporting H2 revenue.

rows.label: Government receivables collection of about INR 100 crore
rows.why: Management is focused on collecting about INR 100 crore of government receivables sooner, with receivable days at 120-122, but no collection timeline was given.

rows.label: Inventory halved and faster supplier payments
rows.why: Management said inventory has been brought down to half and supplier accounts are being settled faster, with cash flows described as strong.

tone.note: Management was confident on EBITDA margin (35%+ for FY27), H2 being better than H1, and the open order book, but evasive on numeric revenue guidance and on the path back to 20%+ growth. Analysts pushed on H2 revenue quantum, receivable days and government collections.
